newsitem.title: USA: Clinton signs bill outlawing computer mischief.
newsitem.headline: Clinton signs bill outlawing computer mischief.

text.p: President Bill Clinton signed a bill Friday outlawing various forms of computer mischief and increase penalties on repeat offenders.

The National Information Infrastructure Protection Act creates federal penalties for theft of computer information across state lines and outlaws the transmission of threats against computer networks across state or international boundries.
"This law is very good news for American businesses and our national security," said Senator Jon Kyl, a sponsor of the measure. "It brings the law up to speed with technology."
The Arizona Republican introduced the measure along with Sen. Patrick Leahy, Democrat of Vermont, and Sen. Charles Grassley, Republican of Iowa.

Hackers have recently broken into government Internet sites, replacing official data with protests against the Communications Decency Act. Last month, the Central Intelligence Agency's World Wide Web page was defaced and renamed the "Central Stupidity Agency" home page.
The new law would also make it a felony to trespass in a computer system and use computer time worth more than $5,000.
